title: Daemon restore-controller composition: real core reducer, quiesce commit, inspect/resume/discard
description:
Objective: land the production daemon restore controller that composes the pieces the recovery chain already has but never wires together. Authored by governor-36019faa on human direction 2026-08-10 from architect-5b5302ee's audit and architect-8ee37119's re-verification on task-b6e3dd2af916490fb2bc4d375a530683.

THE GAP, from architect-5b5302ee's audit blocker 3: "No production daemon restore controller composes verifyBackupGeneration + recovery incarnation + core reducer + SqliteEventStore transaction. recovery.restore_quiesce has NO PRODUCTION CALLER." That last clause is the whole task. @moe/core owns reduceProject(recovery.restore_quiesce) and nothing in production ever calls it, so the reducer is landed-but-uncomposed - exactly the state epic Clause 1 describes when it says exporting symbols is not composition and the runtime-loadability gate proves a package LOADS while nothing proves anything IMPORTS it.

RE-MEASURE BEFORE PLANNING - this description is a snapshot and the staleness rail binds in both directions. In particular confirm that recovery.restore_quiesce still has no production caller; if one has landed since, this task narrows or dies and that is a legitimate outcome to report rather than work around.

WHY THIS IS SEPARATE from task-b6e3dd2a: the anchor installer's owned paths are packages/store/src/recovery-anchor.*, from which apps/daemon is unreachable and must stay unreachable. The composition necessarily lives in the daemon. Merging the two is what made the original task unsatisfiable inside its own scope.

RELATED PRIOR ART to read first: apps/daemon/src/recovery/ already holds recovery-succession.ts, recovery-incarnation.ts, recovery-incarnation-anchor.ts and restart-reconciliation.ts. Establish what each already does before adding a controller; the risk here is a second orchestrator beside an existing one.

NOT IN SCOPE: the two-slot installer protocol (task-b6e3dd2a), the durable key provider, the store schema migration, generating backup bytes, minting entropy or keys, external-effect inventory, R3 completion.

Hard dependencies: the durable OS-protected recovery key provider (order 13.01) AND the store-side recovery binding schema and atomic recovery-install surface (order 13.02) must both be DONE. This task is BACKLOG until then. If claim_next_task serves it early, block it immediately and cite this line rather than re-deriving the chain.

Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/recovery/ - the controller, its .js bridge and focused tests, plus focused export wiring.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test
definitionOfDone: A production restore controller composes verifyBackupGeneration, the recovery incarnation/key surface, the real @moe/core reduceProject(recovery.restore_quiesce) and one SqliteEventStore transaction; a test proves the REAL reducer is invoked rather than a local reimplementation of its policy.
recovery.restore_quiesce has a production caller reachable from the daemon's own entry surface, and a test asserts reachability from that surface rather than by importing the module directly.
The controller commits QUIESCED/RECOVERY_REQUIRED and the installed binding in one transaction; an interrupted run leaves the prior state intact, never a mixed state.

Exact inspect, resume and discard behaviour is owned here: repeated resume of the same prepared command reuses its prepared identity, and a new command for the identical generation requires a different incarnation/key epoch.
Every refusal asserts its exact stable reason code AND the refusing layer; each declared failure injection is generated at least once and a sweep producing zero cases fails the suite.
Mutating each production guard turns a NAMED focused test red; drills run, reverted, exact failing assertion text recorded.
Fresh pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test exits 0.

implementationPlan.note:
EXISTING ORCHESTRATORS MEASURED. restart-reconciliation.ts does NOT perform this composition — the task does not narrow or die.

WHAT restart-reconciliation.ts OWNS (read in full, 250 lines): it takes a set of in-flight ATTEMPTS at daemon restart, calls @moe/runner's classifyCrash on each attempt's situation, maps the classification to a ReconciliationRecord (schema "moe-restart-reconciliation/2"), and commits one row per attempt via store.commitExpectedVersionDecision under commandKind "reconciliation.decide" onto aggregate "restart-reconciliation:<attemptRef>". It never imports @moe/core, never touches reduceProject, never reads or writes the PROJECT aggregate, and never mentions a backup generation or an incarnation.

THE SEAM, stated explicitly as the step demands: restart-reconciliation answers "what happened to each ATTEMPT that was in flight when the process died", per-attempt, on a per-attempt aggregate, with the RUNNER as the deciding authority. The restore controller answers "may this PROJECT quiesce onto a verified backup generation under a fresh incarnation", once, on the PROJECT aggregate (aggregateId === projectId, per bootstrap-sequence.ts:45-48), with the CORE REDUCER as the deciding authority. Different subject, different aggregate, different command kind, different authority. They can both run at boot without either deciding anything the other decides. No second orchestrator.

I ALSO FOUND THE FOLD I MUST COMPOSE RATHER THAN REBUILD — this is the real second-orchestrator hazard and the step's list did not name it. apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/ already owns the durable PROJECT state fold that reduceProject consumes: bootstrap-ledger.ts:119 readDurableLedger(store, projectId) folds only EFFECTS_COMMITTED decisions ("treating a NO_BUSINESS_EFFECT audit row as prior state would let a refusal satisfy a prerequisite"), :176 stateOf(ledger, aggregateId), :172 versionOf(ledger, aggregateId), and bootstrap-sequence.ts:43 aggregateIdFor maps every project.* command to request.projectId. bootstrap-services.ts:41-66 shows the exact production shape — priorProject() then reduceProject() then commit only on acceptance, with refuseFromCore surfacing the core's own code. The restore controller will reuse readDurableLedger/stateOf/versionOf verbatim. Re-deriving project state inside the controller would have been a second fold that could disagree with the one every other project command already uses.

TRANSACTION MECHANISM — I will compose commitWithApply, NOT installRecoveryBinding, and the reason is measurable. sqlite-event-store.ts:287 installRecoveryBinding delegates to recovery-install.ts:118 runInstallTransaction which opens its OWN `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. Called from inside an already-open command transaction that throws (SQLite forbids nesting), so it CANNOT be the "one transaction" DoD 3 requires alongside the lifecycle event. The correct seam is sqlite-event-store.ts:266 commitWithApply(input, apply), documented at event-ledger-transaction.ts:66-69: "Commits the append and `apply` as one transaction. A throwing `apply` rolls the whole append back as PROJECTION_APPLY_FAILED; a replayed command never reaches it." CommitApplyContext (:30) hands the apply the live DatabaseSync inside the open transaction. That is exactly the atomicity DoD 3 asks for, and applyWithinCommit at :129 also refuses a thenable so the apply cannot escape the transaction.

Measured consequence: commitWithApply currently has ZERO production consumers (grep over apps + packages excluding tests returns only its own definition, the decision-ledger delegation and the SqliteEventStore facade). It is a seam built and never wired — the same landed-but-uncomposed shape as restore_quiesce itself.

BINDING CODEC IS COMPOSED, NOT REIMPLEMENTED. encodeRecoveryBinding is root-exported from @moe/store (index.ts:81) and returns { ok, binding, bytes, digest } or a refusal carrying code + layer. The controller will call it for the bytes and digest and only write the row inside the apply. The store's own schema comment sanctions this direction — sqlite-schema-recovery-manifest.ts:6-9: "the daemon maps its RecoveryIncarnationBinding onto these columns, and lifecycle reasoning stays where reduceProject already lives."

RECOVERY-SUCCESSION.TS WILL NOT BE TOUCHED. 369 lines, over target, near the 400 bar. The controller gets its own module.

REFUSAL LAYERS AVAILABLE TO PIN (DoD 5 needs code AND layer): BACKUP_GENERATION — backup-generation-contracts.ts:123 refuseBackupGeneration returns a fixed tuple { code: "BACKUP_PROOF_UNKNOWN", layer: "BACKUP_GENERATION", reason: <varies> }, so the discriminating value is `reason` and I must assert reason + layer, not code alone. implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED — apps/daemon/src/recovery/restore-controller.test.ts, before implementation.

DoD 1's hardest clause: prove the REAL reducer is invoked, not a local reimplementation of its policy. Assert an outcome only reduceProject can produce — drive a command from a lifecycle the reducer REFUSES (project-reducer.ts:35 admits recovery.restore_quiesce only from BOOTSTRAPPING and READY) and assert the controller surfaces that refusal with the reducer's own code. A test that only checks the happy path cannot tell composition from reimplementation, which is the specific defect this task exists to avoid.

DoD 3, the transactional guarantee: assert that an INTERRUPTED run leaves the PRIOR state intact and never a mixed state. Inject the failure between the reducer decision and the commit, then assert BOTH that the lifecycle did not advance AND that no binding was installed. Asserting only one of the two would pass while the other half committed — that is precisely the mixed state DoD 3 forbids.

DoD 4, and it is easy to under-test: repeated resume of the SAME prepared command reuses its prepared identity; a NEW command for the IDENTICAL generation requires a DIFFERENT incarnation/key epoch. Assert both halves. The second is the anti-replay property — same generation plus same epoch must refuse.

DoD 5: every refusal pins its exact stable reason code AND the refusing layer. Each declared failure injection must be GENERATED AT LEAST ONCE and the sweep must assert a non-zero case count — a sweep producing zero cases fails the suite.

Compose real surfaces: the real verifyBackupGeneration, the real incarnation/key surface, the real reduceProject, a real SqliteEventStore over a mkdtemp directory outside the repo, cleaned up in an afterEach that runs on failure (recursive and forced — win32 host).

GREEN 1 — apps/daemon/src/recovery/restore-controller.ts plus its sibling .js bridge. The composition itself.

Compose, in order: verifyBackupGeneration (from the @moe/store root, not a deep import) to establish the generation is intact; the recovery incarnation/key surface via readAnchoredIncarnation / anchorIncarnation and the succession service; then reduceProject with a recovery.restore_quiesce command carrying a RestoreQuiesceWitness assembled from those verified facts; then ONE SqliteEventStore transaction committing the QUIESCED/RECOVERY_REQUIRED outcome and the installed binding together.

DO NOT REIMPLEMENT LIFECYCLE, EPOCH OR DISPOSITION POLICY. The rail names reimplemented authority as the specific defect this task exists to avoid. The controller assembles a witness and asks the reducer; it never decides admissibility itself. If you find yourself writing a lifecycle check that duplicates project-reducer.ts:35, delete it and let the reducer refuse.

RecoveryAnchor stays BOOTSTRAP SELECTION METADATA ONLY — the selected verified database remains the sole lifecycle/readiness authority. Do not let the anchor become a second source of truth for readiness.

Fail closed with stable reason codes and the refusing layer on every path. A fact that cannot be verified is UNKNOWN and refuses; it never defaults to a permissive value.

.js bridge mandatory — its absence fails neither tsc nor vitest and breaks only plain Node. Match the sibling bridges in apps/daemon/src/recovery/, trailing LF included; verify with od -c.

<=250 physical lines measured with `grep -c ''`; split before 400. If inspect/resume/discard will not fit here, put them in the step-5 module rather than growing this file.

GREEN 2 — DoD 4's inspect / resume / discard, in apps/daemon/src/recovery/restore-controller-commands.ts plus its .js bridge, so neither file approaches the cap.

MEASURED VOCABULARY, so you extend rather than collide: `quiesce` and `inspect` have ZERO hits under apps/daemon/src/recovery today — both are new here. `resume` already appears in continuation-contracts.ts and continuation-service.ts, and `discard` in recovery-incarnation.ts and recovery-key-provider.ts. Read those four before naming anything: if an existing resume or discard already means something in this directory, your command must either compose it or be named distinctly. Two different `discard` semantics in one directory is a trap for every later reader.

DoD 4 exactly: repeated resume of the same prepared command REUSES its prepared identity — so prepared identity must be derived deterministically from the command, not minted per call. A new command for the identical generation REQUIRES a different incarnation/key epoch — so the epoch participates in the identity, and same-generation-same-epoch refuses as a replay.

inspect is read-only and must not mutate or advance anything, including as a side effect of reading. Assert that in the test.

Same discipline as step 4: compose the landed surfaces, fail closed with code and layer, <=250 lines, .js bridge with od -c verified trailing LF.

DoD 2 — REACHABILITY FROM THE DAEMON'S OWN ENTRY SURFACE. This is the Clause 1 clause and the reason the task exists; exporting the controller does not satisfy it.

Wire the controller so recovery.restore_quiesce has a production caller reachable from the daemon's entry surface. Read apps/daemon/src/daemon-store-dependencies.ts first — the human's landed-surface inventory records it as the registry that wires runtime kinds through committed services over SqliteEventStore, so it is the likeliest correct seam. Confirm on disk rather than assuming; if the right seam is the HTTP listener or the entry port instead, use that and say why.

THE TEST MUST ASSERT REACHABILITY FROM THAT SURFACE, NOT BY IMPORTING THE MODULE DIRECTLY — DoD 2 says so explicitly. Resolve the controller the way the daemon actually resolves it at runtime, through the registry or entry surface, and assert the call lands. An `import { restoreController }` in the test proves the module exists, which was never in doubt; it does not prove anything imports it in production.

Keep the wiring minimal: one durable call site. This task is the composition, not a new protocol surface — the core contract comment at project-contract.ts:38 is explicit that recovery.restore_quiesce "is not a public protocol command", so do NOT expose it as one over HTTP or MCP.

CROSS-PACKAGE EDGE PROOF, per rail: the daemon already declares @moe/core workspace:* and reduceProject is root-exported at core index.ts:4, so the edge exists. If you add any NEW cross-package import, prove that edge too — manifest entry, lockfile importer, and a compiled bare-specifier probe deleted in the same command. A symbol resolving in tsc is not proof the dependency edge is declared.

DoD 6 MUTATION DRILLS — each production guard must turn a NAMED focused test red. Run each, confirm the named test dies, revert, confirm green, and record the EXACT failing assertion text (DoD 6 asks for the text, not just that it failed).

  1. Replace reduceProject with a local lifecycle check that admits the same states -> the DoD 1 real-reducer test must go RED. If it stays green, that test is asserting a happy path both implementations satisfy, and it proves nothing about composition.
  2. Commit the lifecycle change and the binding install in TWO transactions -> the interrupted-run test must go RED on the mixed-state assertion.
  3. Mint prepared identity per call instead of deriving it -> the repeated-resume test must go RED.
  4. Drop the epoch from the identity so same-generation-same-epoch is accepted -> the replay refusal must go RED.
  5. Let inspect advance state -> the read-only assertion must go RED.
  6. Remove the entry-surface wiring -> the DoD 2 reachability test must go RED while a direct-import test would still pass. This drill is what proves the reachability assertion is real rather than an import in disguise.
  7. Delete a .js bridge -> plain Node breaks while tsc and vitest stay green.

SHARED-WORKTREE HAZARD, which has fired three times this session: a foreign completion hook can whole-tree commit your mutation while it is on disk. After each revert check BOTH `git diff -- <file>` AND `git status --porcelain <file>`; a clean diff alone is not proof.

DoD 7 — VERIFY AND ADVERSARIAL REVIEW. Run the exact gate LAST, fresh and foreground, FROM THE REPO ROOT:

  pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test

Run `pwd` first. The Bash cwd persists across calls and a run from a subdirectory prints a convincing false green — I hit exactly that while measuring this task and read five present symbols as absent. Baseline measured 2026-08-10: apps/daemon was 54 files / 857 tests. Your run must show MORE files; a flat count means your tests never ran.

Path-attributed baseline per global rail 3: record repo-wide failures at merge-base and HEAD, require (HEAD minus merge-base) intersected with owned paths to be EMPTY, disclose foreign red verbatim. Foreign red inside @moe/daemon itself is a BLOCK, not a disclosure.

Adversarial review:
- Did I reimplement lifecycle, epoch or disposition policy anywhere? That is the rail's central prohibition. Any lifecycle check duplicating project-reducer.ts:35 is the defect.
- Is recovery.restore_quiesce reachable from the ENTRY surface, proven without a direct module import?
- Did I hand-roll a transaction instead of composing the store's atomic recovery-install?
- Did the controller become a second orchestrator beside restart-reconciliation.ts? Say in the evidence what the seam is.
- Did RecoveryAnchor become a readiness authority? It must stay bootstrap selection metadata only.
- Did I grow recovery-succession.ts (369 lines, near the 400 bar)? I must not have.
- Does `resume` or `discard` here collide semantically with the existing ones in continuation-service.ts / recovery-incarnation.ts?
- Does every refusal pin the exact code AND the refusing layer, and did every declared injection generate at least one case with a non-zero count?
- Both .js bridges present with od -c verified trailing LF?
- Per-file `grep -c ''` at or below 250, hard bar 400.
- No temp SQLite directory or generated evidence in the diff.

COMMIT BY EXPLICIT PATHSPEC, then run `git diff --cached --name-only` and confirm it is EXACTLY your owned paths. The index on this board is shared and has arrived pre-loaded with foreign files this session; two of my own files were swept into unrelated commits. Never git add -A.

planningNotes.risks:
1. REIMPLEMENTING REDUCER POLICY IN THE DAEMON. The rail names this as the specific defect the task exists to avoid, and it is easy to do by accident — a lifecycle guard in the controller that duplicates project-reducer.ts:35 looks like defensive programming and is actually a second authority. Drill 1 is designed to catch it: a happy-path-only test cannot distinguish composition from reimplementation.

2. A SECOND ORCHESTRATOR. restart-reconciliation.ts already has 12 exports at 250 lines. If it turns out to perform this composition already, the honest outcome is to report the task as narrowed or dead — the description explicitly allows that.

3. HALF-COMMITTED STATE. DoD 3's interrupted-run test must assert BOTH that the lifecycle did not advance AND that no binding was installed. Asserting one alone passes while the other half commits, which is the mixed state being forbidden.

4. PROVING DoD 2 WITH AN IMPORT. An import proves the module exists; it proves nothing about production reachability. Drill 6 exists to prove the reachability test is real.

5. REPLAY VIA IDENTITY MINTING. If prepared identity is minted per call rather than derived, repeated resume silently creates duplicates; if the epoch is left out of identity, same-generation-same-epoch replays are accepted. Both are DoD 4 failures and both look fine in a happy-path test.

6. VOCABULARY COLLISION. `resume` and `discard` already carry meanings in continuation-service.ts and recovery-incarnation.ts. Two different discard semantics in one directory is a trap for every later reader.

7. RecoveryAnchor DRIFTING INTO AUTHORITY. It must remain bootstrap selection metadata; the selected verified database stays the sole lifecycle/readiness authority.

8. GROWING recovery-succession.ts, already 369 lines against a 400 hard bar.

9. A MISSING .js BRIDGE — invisible to tsc and vitest, breaks only plain Node.

10. PERSISTENT BASH CWD producing false negatives, and a shared index that has already swept two of my files into foreign commits this session.
